Lock-level ids move with every admission to app/,\n      # which readers depends on without using it, so they are not compared.\n      - name: the certified bundles were exported from these sources (semantic ids, no Lean)\n        run: |\n          set -euo pipefail\n          # The lexlean cache is keyed by .github/lexlean.pin, so after the pin moves the replay above may have been skipped with no binary restored.\n          cmp -s .github/lexlean.pin target/lexlean/pin || { rm -rf target/lexlean; rustup toolchain install 1.97.0 --profile minimal; RUSTFLAGS=\"--remap-path-prefix=${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}=cargo-home\" cargo +1.97.0 install --locked $(cat .github/lexlean.pin) lexlean --root target/lexlean; cp .github/lexlean.pin target/lexlean/pin; }\n          ll=\"$PWD/target/lexlean/bin/lexlean\"\n          for pair in studio:certified readers:certified-readers readers/xml:certified-xml admit:certified-admit; do\n            project=$(cut -d : -f 1 <<< \"$pair\")\n            bundle=$(cut -d : -f 2 <<< \"$pair\")\n            if [ ! git diff --quiet; then echo \"::error::publish changed $(git diff --name-only | tr '\\n' ' '): run every operation through operate, which ends with check, build and publish\"; exit 1; fi\n      - name: accept the Prism of the seed Verdant Studio, every facet at its media type and its generator's fidelity\n        run: python3 .github/scripts/prism-acceptance.py node target/prismpm/sdk/npm/prism-code/bin/prism-code.mjs\n      - name: next answers within a second, because operate's advance runs it on every push to main\n        run: |\n          set -euo pipefail\n          best=999999\n          for attempt in 1 2 3; do\n            start=$EPOCHREALTIME\n            target/release/verdant_studio next > target/next.txt || true\n            end=$EPOCHREALTIME\n            took=$(( (${end/./} - ${start/./}) / 1000 ))\n            if [ \"$took\" -lt \"$best\" ]; then best=$took; fi\n          done\n          echo \"next took ${best} ms, the best of 3 runs\"\n          if [ \"$best\" -gt 1000 ]; then echo \"::error::next took ${best} ms, over its 1 s budget: make the reads it repeats cheaper before adding more\"; exit 1; fi\n      - if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'\n        uses: actions/cache@5a3ec84eff668545956fd18022155c47e93e2684 # v4.2.3\n        with:\n          path: ~/.elan\n          key: lean-4.32.2-elan-4.1.2\n      - name: run propose-command end to end when the pull request changes the API's own workflows\n        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'\n        env:\n          BASE: ${{ github.base_ref }}\n        run: |\n          set -euo pipefail\n          # The studio check proves the model and replays the certified bundle, but the API's own paths\n          # run in these workflows. So a change to them must pass operate's propose-command step itself,\n          # on a fixture change, and that export must reproduce certified/ byte for byte.\n          git fetch -q --depth=1 origin \"$BASE\"\n          if git diff --quiet FETCH_HEAD -- .github; then echo \"the workflows are main's, which main's own runs exercise\"; exit 0; fi\n          mkdir -p target\n          python3 -c 'import yaml; steps = yaml.safe_load(open(\".github/workflows/operate.yml\"))[\"jobs\"][\"operate\"][\"steps\"]; print([step[\"run\"] for step in steps if step.get(\"name\", \"\").startswith(\"apply a change\")][0])' > target/propose.sh\n          d=dev\n          none=null\n          {\n            echo \"Fixture change for the studio check's end-to-end run of propose-command.\"\n            echo\n            echo \"diff --git a/features/suites/e2e.fixture b/features/suites/e2e.fixture\"\n            echo \"new file mode 100644\"\n            echo \"--- /$d/$none\"\n            echo \"+++ b/features/suites/e2e.fixture\"\n            echo \"@@ -0,0 +1 @@\"\n            echo \"+fixture\"\n          } > target/fixture.patch\n          INPUT=\"$(cat target/fixture.patch)\" bash target/propose.sh\n          rm -f features/suites/e2e.fixture\n          # certified-xml/ and certified-admit/ join the comparison once main holds them: the export that first writes it is the one that adds it.\n          bundles=\"certified certified-readers\"\n          if [ -n \"$(git ls-files certified-xml | head -n 1)\" ]; then bundles=\"$bundles certified-xml\"; fi\n          if [ -n \"$(git ls-files certified-admit | head -n 1)\" ]; then bundles=\"$bundles certified-admit\"; fi\n          if [ -n \"$(git status --porcelain -- $bundles)\" ]; then\n            echo \"::error::operate's propose-command step ran, but its export did not reproduce certified/:\"\n            git status --short -- $bundles | head -20\n            attested=$(git show HEAD:certified/evidence/attestation.json | jq -c .lexlean); used=$(jq -c .lexlean certified/evidence/attestation.json)\n            [ \"$attested\" = \"$used\" ] || echo \"::error::the export ran with lexlean $used, but certified/ attests lexlean $attested. lexlean is built from .github/lexlean.pin with rust 1.97.0 and its cargo home remapped, so a different executable means the toolchain or the runner image changed\"\n            exit 1\n          fi\n          echo \"propose-command applied the fixture, exported again with Lean and reproduced certified/ byte for byte\"\n      - name: accept only pull requests made through the API (last, so every seal step reports first)\n        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'\n        env:\n          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}\n          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}\n          AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}\n        run: |\n          set -euo pipefail\n          app='afflom-verdant-studio[bot]'\n          if [ \"$AUTHOR\" != \"$app\" ]; @10074 := "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Generated by `verdant-studio publish` from studio/src/Studio/Ops.lex.tex. Do not edit.\n# The one Lean export of the certified command. operate's propose-command and refresh both run it,\n# and the studio check runs propose-command end to end, so a change that breaks it fails there.\n# Export time is a requirement: every Lean phase runs under child_timeout_ms (300 s, studio/lexlean.toml),\n# so this script measures each phase and fails at 240 s, 80 percent of that limit, before time can creep up to it.\nset -euo pipefail\nll=\"$1\"\nlog=\"$2\"\nphases=\"$log.phases\"\n: > \"$phases.raw\"\n( while :; do ps -eo etimes=,args= | awk '$2 == \"lean\" && $3 == \"-R\" { m = $NF; sub(\".*-src/\", \"\", m); print $1, m }' >> \"$phases.raw\" || true; sleep 1; done ) &\nwatch=$!\nstatus=0\n# Each LexLean project exports under its own limits: studio, readers, admit and readers/xml when they exist, largest first.\n# Lean's proof of a project grows with the square of its function count, so the readers are split by family and admission is its own project.\n# Each export runs two Lean phases at once, so at most half as many exports as cores run together: more slows every phase.\nslots=$(( $(nproc) / 2 ))\nif [ \"$slots\" -lt 1 ]; then slots=1; fi\nrunning=0\nexported=' '\nfor project in studio readers admit readers/xml; do\n  if [ -f \"$project/lexlean.toml\" ]; then\n    # A project whose semantic id is the one its committed bundle was exported from, under the same lexlean, is not\n    # exported again: the studio check compares exactly these ids, so its bundle stays the bundle of its sources.\n    case \"$project\" in studio) bundle=certified;; readers/xml) bundle=certified-xml;; *) bundle=\"certified-$project\";; esac\n    if [ -f \"$bundle/result.json\" ] && git diff --quiet HEAD -- .github/lexlean.pin; then\n      now=$(cd \"$project\" && \"$ll\" lock >/dev/null && \"$ll\" check | sed -n 's/.*semantic \\([0-9a-f]*\\)).*/\\1/p')\n      if [ -n \"$now\" ] && [ \"$now\" = \"$(jq -r .source.semantic_id \"$bundle/result.json\")\" ]; then\n        echo \"$project is unchanged since $bundle was exported (semantic $now), so it is not exported again\"\n        continue\n      fi\n    fi\n    exported=\"$exported$project \"\n    if [ \"$running\" -ge \"$slots\" ]; then wait -n || status=$?; running=$((running - 1)); fi\n    (cd \"$project\" && \"$ll\" lock && \"$ll\" check && \"$ll\" production build --request production-request.json) > \"$log.${project//\\//-}\" 2>&1 &\n    running=$((running + 1))\n  fi\ndone\nwhile [ \"$running\" -gt 0 ]; do wait -n || status=$?; running=$((running - 1)); done\n: > \"$log\"\nfor part in studio readers readers-xml admit; do\n  if [ -f \"$log.$part\" ]; then cat \"$log.$part\" >> \"$log\"; fi\ndone\nkill \"$watch\" 2> \"$phases.err\" || true\nawk '{ if ($1 > t[$2]) t[$2] = $1 } END { for (m in t) print t[m], m }' \"$phases.raw\" | sort -rn > \"$phases\"\necho \"Lean phases by wall time in seconds, longest first (the limit is 300, and the export fails at 240):\"\nhead -n 8 \"$phases\"\nif [ \"$status\" -ne 0 ]; @17494 := "          # A VS ID this change adds that main already has becomes the next free one, and a pure append is\n          # appended on main instead of patched (prepare-change.py, which refresh runs too).\n          python3 .github/scripts/prepare-change.py prepare target/input/change.patch target/input/appends.json\n          # git apply drops a file whose binary patch is corrupt, says so on one error line and still exits 0, so any error line stops the run here, before the export.\n          # Contract and strata keep their entries on one line, so a change that only adds entries there is merged\n          # into main by entry, and never conflicts with another change that adds others (merge-entries.py).\n          python3 .github/scripts/merge-entries.py patch target/input/change.patch\n          : > target/apply.err\n          if grep -q '^diff --git' target/input/change.patch; then git apply --exclude=studio/lexlean.lock --exclude=readers/lexlean.lock --exclude=readers/xml/lexlean.lock --exclude=admit/lexlean.lock target/input/change.patch 2> target/apply.err || { sed 's/^/::error::/' target/apply.err; exit 1; }; fi\n          if grep -q '^error' target/apply.err; then sed 's/^/::error::the patch did not apply whole: /' target/apply.err; exit 1; fi\n          python3 .github/scripts/prepare-change.py append target/input/appends.json\n"

@19292 := "            # The repair of a merge that broke the API's own path. Dispatched from a branch at the last\n"

@19310 := @539 @19308 @512
@19311 := @727 @19310
@19312 := @539 @19311
@19313 := "            case \"$merge\" in *[!0-9a-f]*|'') echo \"::error::revert-merge takes the full hex id of a merge commit on main\"; exit 1;; esac\n"

@19368 := @539 @19367

@19436 := @539 @19434 @512
@19437 := @727 @19436
@19438 := @539 @19437

@19464 := @539 @19462 @512
@19465 := @727 @19464
@19466 := @539 @19465

@19469 := @728 @19468
@19471 := @539 @19469 @512
@19472 := @727 @19471
@19473 := @539 @19472
@19474 := "          MSG\n"

@19478 := @539 @19476 @512
@19479 := @727 @19478
@19480 := @539 @19479
@19481 := "          branch=\"studio/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}\"\n"
@19482 := @729 @19481
@19483 := @728 @19482
@19485 := @539 @19483 @512
@19486 := @727 @19485
@19487 := @539 @19486
@19488 := "          if ! git push origin \"HEAD:refs/heads/${branch}\" 2> target/push.err; then\n"
@19489 := @729 @19488
@19490 := @728 @19489
@19492 := @539 @19490 @512
@19493 := @727 @19492
@19494 := @539 @19493
@19495 := "            grep -E 'GH013|error|rejected|path:' target/push.err | head -20 | sed 's/^/::error::/'\n"
@19496 := @729 @19495

@19499 := @539 @19497 @512

@19502 := "          title=\"verdant_studio $ARGS\"\n"
@19503 := @729 @19502
@19504 := @728 @19503
@19506 := @539 @19504 @512
@19507 := @727 @19506
@19508 := @539 @19507
@19509 := "          if [ \"$ARGS\" = propose-command ]; then title=\"verdant_studio propose-command: $(grep -m 1 '[[:alnum:]]' target/summary.md | awk '{ sub(\"^[# ]*\", \"\"); print }')\"; fi\n"

@19513 := @539 @19511 @512
@19514 := @727 @19513
@19515 := @539 @19514
@19516 := "          if [ \"${ARGS#revert-merge }\" != \"$ARGS\" ]; then title=\"verdant_studio propose-command: Revert ${ARGS#revert-merge }, a merge that broke the API's own path\"; fi\n"
@19517 := @729 @19516
@19518 := @728 @19517
@19520 := @539 @19518 @512
@19521 := @727 @19520
@19522 := @539 @19521
@19523 := "          # REST, not GraphQL: run 45646779790 lost its pull request to four GraphQL errors.\n"
@19524 := @729 @19523
@19525 := @728 @19524
@19527 := @539 @19525 @512
@19528 := @727 @19527
@19529 := @539 @19528
@19530 := "          # Opening is idempotent: run 45649684941 opened #263 although its call reported an error, and the retry then failed on \"already exists\".\n"
@19531 := @729 @19530
@19532 := @728 @19531
@19534 := @539 @19532 @512
@19535 := @727 @19534
@19536 := @539 @19535
@19537 := "          # So each try first looks for an open pull request from this branch, and an existing one counts as opened.\n"
@19538 := @729 @19537
@19539 := @728 @19538
@19541 := @539 @19539 @512
@19542 := @727 @19541
@19543 := @539 @19542
@19544 := "          pr=\"\"\n"

@19546 := @728 @19545
@19548 := @539 @19546 @512
@19549 := @727 @19548
@19550 := @539 @19549
@19551 := "          for try in 1 2 3 4; do\n"
@19552 := @729 @19551
@19553 := @728 @19552
@19555 := @539 @19553 @512
@19556 := @727 @19555
@19557 := @539 @19556

@19559 := @729 @19558
@19560 := @728 @19559
@19562 := @539 @19560 @512
@19563 := @727 @19562
@19564 := @539 @19563

@19566 := @729 @19565
@19567 := @728 @19566
@19569 := @539 @19567 @512
@19570 := @727 @19569
@19571 := @539 @19570
@19572 := "            if pr=$(command gh api \"repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pulls\" -f head=\"$branch\" -f base=main -f title=\"$title\" -F body=@target/operation.txt --jq .number) && [ -n \"$pr\" ]; then break; fi\n"
@19573 := @729 @19572

@19578 := @539 @19577

@19583 := @539 @19581 @512

@19585 := @539 @19584

@19590 := @539 @19588 @512
@19591 := @727 @19590

@19597 := @539 @19595 @512

@19606 := @539 @19605

@19608 := @729 @19607
@19609 := @728 @19608
@19611 := @539 @19609 @512
@19612 := @727 @19611
@19613 := @539 @19612
@19614 := "          gh api \"repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/rules/branches/main\" > target/rules.json\n"
@19615 := @729 @19614
@19616 := @728 @19615
@19618 := @539 @19616 @512
@19619 := @727 @19618
@19620 := @539 @19619
@19621 := "          # A change to the API itself (propose-command, revert-merge) merges as every App pull request does:\n"
@19622 := @729 @19621

@19625 := @539 @19623 @512
@19626 := @727 @19625
@19627 := @539 @19626

@19629 := @729 @19628

@19632 := @539 @19630 @512
@19633 := @727 @19632

@19636 := @729 @19635
@19637 := @728 @19636
@19639 := @539 @19637 @512
@19640 := @727 @19639
@19641 := @539 @19640

@19646 := @539 @19644 @512
@19647 := @727 @19646

@19655 := @539 @19654

@19661 := @727 @19660

@19667 := @539 @19665 @512
@19668 := @727 @19667

@19674 := @539 @19672 @512
@19675 := @727 @19674

@19681 := @539 @19679 @512
@19682 := @727 @19681

@19706 := @729 @19705
